title: The reduction tower of an integral complex does not depend on the K-flat resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a scheme $Y$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with projections $\pi_n:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{E,n})_Y$, let $\rho_n:(A_{E,n+1})_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the reduction maps, so that $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$, and let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived category of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]; let $\operatorname{Res}_n:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived restriction of scalars [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars].

Let $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, and let $q:P\to K$ and $q':P'\to K$ be quasi-isomorphisms from K-flat complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $n\geq1$ put $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $P'_n=P'\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y$ (termwise change of rings along $\pi_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), read as complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules via $\pi_n$; let $\gamma_n:P\to P_n$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and $\tau_n=\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\rho_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ be the resulting morphisms of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules, and $\gamma'_n,\tau'_n$ the same for $P'$. Let $\theta_n:P_n\to P'_n$ be the canonical isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ between the two computations of the derived change of rings along $\pi_n$ given by the K-flat resolutions $q$ and $q'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, clause 2]. Then:

1. $\operatorname{Res}_n(\theta_n)\circ[\gamma_n]\circ[q]^{-1}=[\gamma'_n]\circ[q']^{-1}$ as morphisms $K\to\operatorname{Res}_n(P'_n)$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$;
2. $\operatorname{Res}_n(\theta_n)\circ[\tau_n]=[\tau'_n]\circ\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(\theta_{n+1})$ as morphisms $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(P_{n+1})\to\operatorname{Res}_n(P'_n)$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$.

So the inverse systems $(\operatorname{Res}_nP_n,[\tau_n])_n$ and $(\operatorname{Res}_nP'_n,[\tau'_n])_n$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, together with their maps from $K$, are isomorphic through $(\operatorname{Res}_n\theta_n)_n$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Modules on Sites, Section 'Flat resolutions' (Tag 06YL) and Section 'Derived pullback' (Tag 06YV): the derived change of rings is computed by K-flat resolutions, and the comparison isomorphisms are natural in the resolution; the compatibility with the maps x -> x⊗1 and id⊗ρ_n is written out by no source (it is what makes the 'natural map K -> R lim(K⊗^L R/m^n)' of Bhatt-Scholze p. 24, Proposition 3.5.1/Definition 3.5.2, independent of choices)
